subject: chemistry
title: Atom economy
key_idea: Atom economy measures how much of the starting materials end up as the useful product. It is calculated from the balanced equation. A high atom economy means less waste, so it matters for sustainable development and for cost.

blocks.text: (Chemistry only) Most reactions make a useful product and also by-products. Atom economy shows how much of the reactants become the product you want.

items.meaning: A measure of the amount of starting materials that end up as useful products.
The product the reaction is carried out to make.

items: It is important for sustainable development, because it makes the best use of raw materials.
It is important for economic reasons, because less starting material ends up as waste.
A reaction that makes only the desired product has an atom economy of 100%.
Atom economy is the percentage of the starting materials that end up as useful product.
Reactions with a high atom economy make less waste and use raw materials better.

blocks.text: Use the balanced equation. Multiply each relative formula mass by the number in front of that formula.

blocks.label: Percentage atom economy
blocks.formula: atom economy = Mr of desired product ÷ sum of Mr of all reactants × 100
where: Mr of desired product is the relative formula mass from the equation
sum of Mr of all reactants is the total from the equation

items.text: Add up the Mr of all the reactants in the equation.
Find the Mr of the product you want, allowing for the number in front.
Divide the Mr of the desired product by the total Mr of the reactants, then multiply by 100.

blocks.text: Example: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. The desired product is CaO. Mr: CaCO₃ = 100, CaO = 56. Atom economy = 56 ÷ 100 × 100 = 56%.

items: The total Mr of all the reactants equals the total Mr of all the products, because no atoms are lost.
So the total Mr of the products can be used in the denominator instead.
Give the answer to the number of significant figures asked for.

diagram.alt: Practise calculating a percentage atom economy from relative formula masses.
diagram.question: In a reaction, the desired product has an Mr of **{d}**. The sum of the Mr of all the reactants in the equation is **{r}**. Calculate the percentage atom economy.
working: Atom economy = Mr of desired product ÷ sum of Mr of all reactants × 100.

items: Atom economy = Mr of desired product ÷ total Mr of reactants × 100.
Multiply each Mr by the number in front of the formula in the balanced equation.

blocks.text: (Higher tier) Atom economy is only one factor. A pathway is chosen using data such as atom economy, yield, rate, equilibrium position and usefulness of by-products.

diagram.alt: Atom economy compared with percentage yield.

values: Mr of desired product with Mr of all reactants
Actual mass of product with theoretical mass
How much of the reactants becomes useful product
How much product was actually obtained

items: Usefulness of the by-products, which can be sold rather than wasted.
Cost of the raw materials and the energy requirement.
Atom economy is a measure from the equation. Percentage yield is a measure from an experiment.
Choose a pathway by weighing atom economy, yield, rate, equilibrium position, by-products and cost.

checks.q: Calculate the atom economy for making calcium oxide from calcium carbonate. CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. Mr: CaCO₃ = 100, CaO = 56.
Give two reasons why it is important to use reactions with a high atom economy.
checks.a: It is important for sustainable development (makes better use of raw materials) and for economic reasons (less waste, so lower costs).

checks.q: Give two factors, other than atom economy, that are considered when choosing a reaction pathway.
checks.a: Any two from: percentage yield, rate of reaction, equilibrium position, usefulness of by-products, cost of raw materials, energy requirement.

mistakes.wrong: Atom economy of nickel = 59 ÷ 75 × 100 = 78.7%, using only NiO as the reactant.
mistakes.right: Use the total Mr of all the reactants. For NiO + C, the total is 75 + 12 = 87, so the atom economy is 59 ÷ 87 × 100 = 67.8%.
Multiply by 100 to give a percentage: 235 × 100 ÷ 320 = 73.4%.

mistakes.wrong: Atom economy of silver iodide = 235 ÷ 170 × 100, using only one reactant.
mistakes.right: The total Mr of both reactants is 170 + 150 = 320. Divide the Mr of AgI by 320.

worked_example.question:
The equation for the reaction is:

AgNO₃(aq) + NaI(aq) → AgI(s) + NaNO₃(aq)

Relative formula masses (Mr): AgNO₃ = 170, NaI = 150, AgI = 235, NaNO₃ = 85

Calculate the percentage atom economy for the production of silver iodide in this reaction.

Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
worked_example.tip: One mark each. The total is found by adding the Mr of both reactants, or both products.

mistakes.right: 63.5 is the Ar of copper. The desired product is SO₂, so use 64 ÷ 191 × 100 = 34%.
The fraction is upside down. Atom economy cannot be more than 100%. Use 414 ÷ 458 × 100 = 90%.
Do not double the total. Add each reactant once, allowing for the number in front of each formula.

worked_example.question:
Lead can be obtained by heating its oxide with carbon.
The balanced equation for the reaction is

2PbO + C → 2Pb + CO₂

Calculate the atom economy for the production of lead in this reaction.
(relative atomic masses: C = 12, O = 16, Pb = 207
relative formula masses: PbO = 223, CO₂ = 44)

Give your answer to two significant figures.
worked_example.tip: A final answer of 90 scores all four marks. Allow for the numbers in front of PbO and Pb.

exam_phrases: atom economy = total Mr of desired products / total Mr of all products x 100
atom economy = total Mr of desired products / total Mr of all reactants x 100

mistakes.right: 6 ÷ 34 × 100 = 17.647…, which is 17.6% to 3 significant figures. 17.7% is not allowed.

mistakes.wrong: The cost of the equipment and plant is another factor in choosing a pathway.
mistakes.right: Cost of equipment, plant or manufacturing, and safety, are ignored. Give cost of raw materials, energy requirement, yield, usefulness of by-products, rate or equilibrium position.

mistakes.wrong: Another factor is the length of time for the reaction.
mistakes.right: This is ignored. Say the rate of reaction.

worked_example.question:
This is the equation for the reaction in an experiment.

NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O

Water is a waste product in this reaction.

Calculate the atom economy for the reaction.

Relative atomic mass (Ar): H = 1.0   O = 16.0   Na = 23.0   Cl = 35.5
answer_points: Mr of NaCl = 58.5 and Mr of H₂O = 18.0 (the total of both products is 76.5).
worked_example.tip: An answer of 76, 76.47 or 76.5 scores all three marks. Desired product on top, total of all products (or reactants) below.
